heading_path.h3: Worked example 11.6: Solving an equation with variables on both sides

records.raw_html:
Worked example 11.6: Solving an equation with variables on both sides

Solve the following equation:

  1. Option 1: Use the additive inverse of a term with a variable to add or subtract it from both sides. We will start on the left-hand side.

  2. Option 2: We will also use the additive inverse, but starting on the right-hand side.
records.answer_text:
Option 1: Use the additive inverse of a term with a variable to add or subtract it from both sides. We will start on the left-hand side.

$$
\begin{align}
18-5x\; \color{red}{+\;5x}&=4x \; \color{red}{+\;5x} \\
18 &= 9x \\
\frac{18}{9}&=\frac{9x}{9} \\
2&=x \\
\therefore x&=2
\end{align}
$$

Option 2: We will also use the additive inverse, but starting on the right-hand side.

$$
\begin{align}
18-5x\; \color{red}{-\;4x}&=4x \; \color{red}{-\;4x} \\
18-9x &= 0 \\
18-9x\; \color{green}{+\;9x}&=0+ \color{green}{9x} \\
18&=9x \\
\frac{18}{9}&=\frac{9x}{9} \\
2&=x \\
\therefore x&=2
\end{align}
$$

records.prompt_text: The length of a rectangle with a perimeter of 120 cm is 10 cm longer than its breadth. Determine the length and the breadth of the rectangle in centimetres.
records.answer_text:
Step 1: Understand the problem.

- Given: $P$ = 120 cm
- Given: Length equals breadth plus 10 cm
- Asked: Length in cm
- Asked: Breadth in cm

Step 2: Devise a plan, which includes expressing all your unknown values in terms of a variable.

- Breadth: $x$
- Length: $x+10$
- For a rectangle: $P=2l+2b$

The equation is:

$$
120=2(x+10)+2(x)
$$

Step 3: Carry out the plan.

$$
\begin{align}
120 &= 2(x+10) + 2x  \\
120 &= 2x + 20 +2x \\
120 &= 4x + 20 \\
120-20 &= 4x+20-20 \\
100&=4x \\
\frac{100}{4}&=\frac{4x}{4} \\
\therefore 25&=x
\end{align}
$$

Therefore:

$$
\begin{align}
\text{Breadth} &= 25\text{ cm}  \\
\text{Length}\phantom{0} &= 25+10 \\
&=35\text{ cm} \\
\end{align}
$$

Step 4: Look back to check.

$$
\begin{align}
120 &= 2(x+10) + 2x \\
120 &= 2(25+10) +2(25) \\
120&=2(35)+50 \\
120&=70+50 \\
120&=120 \\
\therefore \text{LHS}&=\text{RHS}
\end{align}
$$

The length is 35 cm and the breadth is 25 cm.

\frac{1}{4}x&=55 \\

\therefore x &= 220
\end{align}
$$

The full distance is 220 m.

records.prompt_text:
### Exercise 11.5: Use equations to solve problems

4. The sum of three consecutive numbers is 36. Determine the three numbers.
records.answer_text:
Let the first number be $x$. Then the second number is $x+1$, and the third number is $x+2$.

$$
\begin{align}
x+(x+1)+(x+2) &=36 \\
x+x+1+x+2 &= 36 \\
3x+3 &=36 \\
3x+3-3&=36-3 \\
3x&=33 \\
\frac{3x}{3} &= \frac{33}{3} \\
\therefore x &= 11 \\
x+1 &= 12 \\
\text{and }x+2 &=13
\end{align}
$$

The numbers are 11, 12 and 13.

A two-dimensional (2D) shape has two dimensions that we can measure: we can measure the length and we can measure the breadth (sometimes called the width) of the shape. For example, a square is a 2D shape. All the sides of a square are straight lines. A circle is also a 2D shape, but a circle has a curved edge.

We use a special name for the 2D shapes that are formed by straight lines. They are called polygons. We name polygons by counting the number of straight sides that they have. A polygon with five sides is called a pentagon and a polygon with six sides is a hexagon.

There is a whole group of polygons with four sides, and they are the quadrilaterals. You have worked with squares, rectangles, parallelograms, rhombuses and trapeziums before. All of them are examples of quadrilaterals.
